business: An open-source database team run as an autonomous software business (stand-in data: public Apache Cassandra Jira history)
engine: Theory of Constraints flow engine (github.com/khrisdidukh/throughput-treasury/engine), deterministic, reproducible from this snapshot

flow.headline: 46% of delivered work's lead time is waiting in "Open" — a policy constraint. Best move: Decide faster at "Open": owner + SLA + WIP limit (halve the wait) (€926k/year).

evidence: delivered items spent 46% of their lead time waiting in "Open" (80.5 days per item on average)
85% of waits in "Open" were shorter than 25 days — the long tail is where the time goes
the queue was stable (2037 items on average)
"In Progress" works at 66% of its demonstrated capacity (5.8 of 9 items/week) — it has room, so the wait is a decision, not a lack of hands
2011 items have sat here for more than 180 days (aged inventory)
delivered items spent 25% of their lead time waiting in "Triage Needed" (43.3 days per item on average)
85% of waits in "Triage Needed" were shorter than 47 days — the long tail is where the time goes
the queue grew 18% over the period
649 items have sat here for more than 180 days (aged inventory)
delivered items spent 13% of their lead time waiting in "Patch Available" (23.4 days per item on average)
85% of waits in "Patch Available" were shorter than 21 days — the long tail is where the time goes
the queue was stable (104 items on average)
"Review In Progress" works at 65% of its demonstrated capacity (10.4 of 16 items/week) — it has room, so the wait is a decision, not a lack of hands
89 items have sat here for more than 180 days (aged inventory)

adizes.meaning: Entrepreneuring gap — nobody decides quickly what to start and what to drop. Name an intake owner, set a triage SLA and a WIP limit, prune the backlog.
evidence: work waits in "Open" although "In Progress" has spare capacity — a decision is missing, not people
34% of resolved items were closed without ever entering active work — late "no" decisions
2921 items untouched for 180+ days — about 208 weeks of output parked in the backlog

options.action: Decide faster at "Open": owner + SLA + WIP limit (halve the wait)
options.verdict: Real gain: throughput 14.0→16.0 items/week, average lead time 177→137 days.

options.action: Automate half of the work in "In Progress"
options.verdict: Real gain: throughput 14.0→14.0 items/week, average lead time 177→170 days.

options.action: Free one person from "Review In Progress" (runs at 65%)
options.verdict: Real saving: "Review In Progress" has spare capacity, so one person can move to other work without slowing delivery.

options.action: Automate half of "Review In Progress" (the obvious target)
options.verdict: Automation on paper: "Review In Progress" is not where work waits, so ~56 freed hours/week barely change delivery. They turn into money only if those people move to "In Progress" or the cost is actually removed.

options.action: Move one person from "Review In Progress" to "In Progress"
options.verdict: Little effect: work waits for a decision in "Open", not for capacity in "In Progress" (it runs at 66%). More hands won't move it.

options.action: Hire one more person for "In Progress"
options.verdict: Little effect: work waits for a decision in "Open", not for capacity in "In Progress" (it runs at 66%). More hands won't move it.

dataQuality: 32% of status changes were bulk updates (within 2 minutes of the previous one). Time-in-status is approximate where the board is updated after the fact.
34% of resolved items never entered an active status — either closed without work or the workflow is skipped.
